name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,314

entries.clue: Sane arbiter resolves tricky problem (5,6)

indicatorNotes.resolves: to resolve is to break something down and settle it anew, so the letters are broken up and settled into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of SANE ARBITER rearranged

annotation.surface: A level-headed referee settles a thorny dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: "Resolves" reads as the arbiter's verb, with "tricky problem" as its object; in fact it is the instruction working on the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A brainteaser is a puzzle, a tricky problem set for fun.

entries.clue: Adopting new name, purchase pet (5)

indicatorNotes.Adopting: to adopt is to take in, so the purchase word takes the two letters inside it

blocks.note: purchase = BUY, opened up to hold the next letters
N is the standard abbreviation for new
N is the standard abbreviation for name

annotation.surface: A family adopts a pet and gives it a new name as soon as they buy it.
annotation.walkthrough: The two N's sit side by side inside BUY.
annotation.definitionFit: A bunny is a rabbit, a common children's pet.

entries.clue: Maybe spider-like broken anchor secured with help (9)

indicatorNotes.broken: something broken is in pieces, and the pieces of ANCHOR are put back in another order
indicatorNotes.secured with: the scrambled anchor is held fast inside the word for help

blocks.note: help = AID, split to hold the scrambled anchor
the letters of ANCHOR rearranged

annotation.surface: A nautical scene: a broken anchor lashed in place with outside help.
annotation.walkthrough: "Maybe" is part of the definition: arachnoid means spider-like, and it may also name the membrane round the brain, so the setter hedges.
annotation.definitionFit: Arachnoid means resembling a spider or its web.

entries.clue: Want to bite heads off some toys, like Russian dolls? (6)

indicatorNotes.to bite: biting takes something between the teeth, so the word for want closes round the letters
indicatorNotes.heads off: the heads of words are their first letters, taken off them

blocks.note: want = NEED, opened to take in the bite
the first letters (heads) of Some and Toys

annotation.surface: A child longs to chew the heads off a set of Russian dolls.
annotation.walkthrough: Russian dolls (matryoshkas) fit one inside another, which the answer describes, and the clue's own construction does the same thing: ST nests inside NEED.
annotation.definitionFit: Russian dolls sit each inside the next, which is to say nested.

entries.clue: English, repeatedly bowled, decline (3)

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled, here twice

annotation.surface: An English cricket team keeps getting bowled out and goes into a slump.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is bowled when the ball hits the stumps; scorecards write it as b.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tide ebbs as it falls away, and anything that declines can be said to ebb.

entries.clue: Pushing succeeded, glutton grabbing French wine (7)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: the glutton grabs the wine, holding it inside

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
glutton = HOG, split to hold the wine
VIN is French for wine

annotation.surface: A greedy diner elbows through the crowd to snatch a bottle of French wine.
annotation.walkthrough: S for succeeded comes from genealogies and lists of monarchs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with shoving the rougher, more forceful kind of pushing.

entries.clue: Happy occasion — landlord cuts half of rent on June 6, 1944 (3,6,3)

indicatorNotes.cuts: the landlord cuts into D-DAY, landing between its two parts
indicatorNotes.half of: the first half of the word rent is kept

blocks.note: the first two of RENT's four letters
the date of the Normandy landings, D-DAY, split after its D
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

annotation.surface: A landlord marks D-Day by halving the rent, which the tenants celebrate.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface the landlord is a person; as wordplay he is one who lets, and the date is just the Normandy landings, cut open by that word.
annotation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a memorable happy occasion, from saints' days printed in red in old calendars.

entries.clue: Old guard fret about juvenile miscreant (6,6)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean around, turned round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters of OLD GUARD FRET rearranged

annotation.surface: Veteran conservatives worry about a young delinquent.
annotation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the teenage pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; the name has become a byword for any young rogue.
annotation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is literature's best-known juvenile miscreant.

entries.clue: Alerts broadcast about northern available properties (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters of alerts are scattered
indicatorNotes.about: the scrambled letters go round the next one

blocks.note: the letters of ALERTS rearranged, opened to take a letter
N is the standard abbreviation for northern

annotation.surface: A news bulletin announces which homes in the north are up for rent.
annotation.walkthrough: "Broadcast" looks like the news, but it is only the scrambling instruction for ALERTS.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: homes and flats offered for let are listed as rentals.

entries.clue: Wide secondary thoroughfare (5)

blocks.note: B marks the second grade, as with a B-list or B-movie
a thoroughfare is a road

annotation.surface: A description of a broad minor road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a B-road, the British name for a secondary road, and that is exactly how the pieces split.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a broad river is a wide one.

entries.clue: The Reverend’s reserved vessels, more than one circular (9)

indicatorNotes.The Reverend’s: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: reserved = SHY, vessels = FLEETS; swap their opening sounds SH and FL

annotation.surface: A clergyman keeps his own set of vessels, and more than one of them is round.
annotation.walkthrough: "The Reverend" names Spooner without spelling him out. "Circular" looks like an adjective describing the vessels; it is the noun, a handout.
annotation.definitionFit: Flysheets are handbills or leaflets, the same as circulars.

entries.clue: Beach resident’s husband in urgent run in taxi (5,4)

indicatorNotes.in: each small piece goes in the word that follows it

blocks.note: urgent = SORE, as in a sore need, opened for the husband
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
taxi = CAB, opened for the run
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

annotation.surface: A resort resident's husband is rushed off urgently in a taxi.
annotation.walkthrough: SORE for urgent is old-fashioned, as in "in sore need". The two containers are built separately and placed side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: The shore crab is the common crab of beaches and rock pools.

entries.clue: Fish going under keels, essentially (3)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letter

blocks.note: one going under anaesthetic drops below awareness into the unconscious, the ID
the middle letter of KEELS

annotation.surface: A fish swims beneath the hulls of boats.
annotation.walkthrough: The link from "going under" to ID is loose: it points to the unconscious mind that takes over under anaesthesia. The E is the certain part.
annotation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

entries.clue: See result of voting back in lounge (6)

indicatorNotes.back: going back runs the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: LO is an old word for look or see
a poll is the count of votes

annotation.surface: An instruction to go and check the election results in a hotel lounge.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lounge" looks like a room; it is the verb. Only the POLL is reversed, not LO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of lazing: to lollop is to loaf about or sprawl.

entries.clue: I’m spotted in dance outfit after change of heart (7)

annotation.definition: I’m spotted in dance outfit after change of heart
annotation.definitionNote: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: a leopard says "I'm spotted".

indicatorNotes.change of heart: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and here it is changed for another

blocks.note: a leotard is a dancer's one-piece outfit
LEOTARD's middle letter T is changed to P

annotation.surface: Someone confesses to being caught in a leotard after changing their mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue does not say where the new P comes from; any single-letter swap at the centre that makes a word will do, and the spots confirm it. "Spotted" in the surface means seen.
annotation.definitionFit: The leopard is the big cat famous for its spots.

entries.clue: Leave behind fake centrepiece for altar (6)

indicatorNotes.centrepiece for: the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: to fake is to forge
the middle letter of ALTAR

annotation.surface: Someone abandons a counterfeit decoration for a church altar.
annotation.walkthrough: "Centrepiece" suggests an ornament on the altar, but it only asks for ALTAR's middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To forget something is to leave it behind by accident, as with an umbrella.

entries.clue: Something under fire has exploded mine (3,3)

indicatorNotes.exploded: an explosion blows things apart, and the letters of has land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of HAS rearranged
a coal mine is a pit

annotation.surface: A soldier under fire reports that a mine has gone off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Under fire" reads as under attack; it is literal, the pit beneath a grate or furnace.
annotation.definitionFit: An ash pit sits under a fire to catch the ashes.

entries.clue: I’m surprised nothing accompanies hot duck (3)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a sentence meaning what the exclamation expresses.

indicatorNotes.accompanies: to accompany is to go along with, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: A diner is startled to find nothing served with the hot duck.
annotation.walkthrough: "Duck" looks like the dish; in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so it gives O like "nothing" does.
annotation.definitionFit: The exclamation stands for the whole sentence: saying oho announces that you are surprised.

entries.clue: What could make pets ultimately seem dire? (9)

annotation.definition: What could make pets ultimately seem dire?

indicatorNotes.could make: the letters could be made into the answer, rearranged
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of seem is used

blocks.note: PETS + M (last of SEEM) + DIRE, rearranged

annotation.surface: A question about what could make pets' health look dire.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: distemper is a disease that makes pets gravely ill.
annotation.definitionFit: Distemper is a viral disease of dogs and other animals that can make them seriously ill.

entries.clue: Strong acid may score this buzz (5)

annotation.definitionNote: "Buzz" is the verb, as in give someone a buzz.

blocks.note: strong acids sit at the very bottom of the pH scale, so read the reading as letters plus a number word
to give someone a buzz is to call them

annotation.surface: A strong acid can etch something, and it fizzes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Score" looks like scratch; here it is the reading an acid gets on the pH scale, where 1 is very acidic. Split the answer as PH ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: Buzz is informal for a phone call; the acid half is cryptic, since a strong acid scores pH 1 on the scale.

entries.clue: Good girl’s mirror (5)

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl

annotation.surface: A well-behaved girl's looking glass.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for "is", joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An older word: a looking-glass, or just a glass, is a mirror.

entries.clue: Dubois regularly raised very small amount of cash (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down answer, raising the letters writes them bottom to top

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of DUBOIS

annotation.surface: Someone named Dubois scraped together a tiny sum of money.
annotation.walkthrough: The sou was an old French coin of little value, so it stands for a trifling sum, and the French name Dubois fits the theme.
annotation.definitionFit: A sou was a low-value French coin, now used for a very small amount of money.

entries.clue: Eg polar rocks on which climbers develop (7)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes the answer instead of naming it: a structure that climbing plants grow on.

indicatorNotes.rocks: to rock is to shake, and shaken letters settle in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of EG POLAR rearranged

annotation.surface: Polar rock faces are where mountaineers build their skills.
annotation.walkthrough: "Climbers" suggests mountaineers and "rocks" their crags; the climbers are plants, and "rocks" is the scrambling instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework over which climbing plants are trained.

entries.clue: Valiant Bill to intensify checks (11)

indicatorNotes.checks: to check is to hold back, so the word for intensify holds the bill inside

blocks.note: to intensify = REDOUBLE, split to hold the bill
a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

annotation.surface: A brave legislator's bill would tighten inspections.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bill" looks like a law or a man's name; it is the tab. "Checks" looks like inspections but means holds in.
annotation.definitionFit: Redoubtable means formidable, especially as an opponent, which is close to valiant.
